newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Eletrobras sees higher rates boosting revs.
newsitem.headline: Eletrobras sees higher rates boosting revs.

text.p: Brazil's latest electricity rate restructuring will boost estimated revenues at federally owned power company Eletrobras by 1.5 billion reais this year, the company's president said on Tuesday.
Eletrobras President Firmino Sampaio told reporters that the company previously had estimated 1997 revenues would reach 19 billion reais.
The government announced on Monday an average 9.92 percent increase in tariffs in the second electricity rate restructuring since November 1995 to eliminate cross subsidies.

On Tuesday, the Mines and Energy Ministry announced a breakdown of rate increases for Eletrobras units, including 13.57 percent and 14.8 percent increases in tariffs charged by the Furnas and Eletrosul generating units, respectively.
The ministry has not announced rate increases for Eletrobras' Eletronorte and Chesf, Firmino added.
He said electrical consumption in Brazil would grow 5.1 percent this year, adding consumption grew six percent in the first two months of the year.
To meet demand, Eletrobras plans to invest $7 billion this year in thermoelectric projects and energy purchases from Argentina.
